clue.text: No.1 from Neil Diamond literally emptied well

indicators.note: the number one letter, the first, is taken from the word Neil

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of the word literally is removed, leaving its two outer letters

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint that a Neil Diamond chart-topper drained a well dry, word for word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neil Diamond' reads as the American singer-songwriter, but the two names do separate jobs; 'emptied well' sounds like a drained water source, yet 'well' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in a satisfactory or pleasing manner, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Clue not designed for 1 in 10

indicators.note: designed means the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A setter admits a clue was not meant to fit the space at 1 in 10.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 in 10' reads as a cross-reference: this answer, 1, is a member of the 10 across order of bats.
explanation.definitionFit: This large European bat is one species within the bat order, so it is an example of it.

clue.text: Obscure collective noun for 25?

definitions.meaning: to obscure is to hide or blur from view
a group of bats in flight is traditionally called by this word, as a flock is for birds

explanation.surface: A puzzle about an obscure name for a group of bats.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to make unclear, and as a noun it is the term for a swarm of bats.

clue.text: Nurse endlessly upset about the start of Trading Places

indicators.note: about means the reversed name goes round the other letter
upset in a down clue means the name is turned upside down, read backwards
endlessly means the final letter of the nurse's name is dropped

parts.note: Mary Seacole was the Jamaican-British nurse of the Crimean War

indicators.note: the start of means the first letter of the word Trading

explanation.surface: A nurse, upset about something, swaps jobs in the film Trading Places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SEACOLE to SEACOL; 'upset' turns it to LOCAES, which goes 'about' T.
explanation.definitionFit: Places and finds both mean puts something in a position or discovers where it is, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of SW London where 25 may roost reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the clue's description is heard rather than spelt, matching a district name

parts.note: farm buildings, barns, are where bats (25) often roost

explanation.surface: A local guide notes which London district bats might choose to settle in.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNES is a riverside district of south-west London; 25 is BATS, and bats roost in barns, which sounds like the district.
explanation.definitionFit: The district is an area in the London borough of Richmond upon Thames, south-west of the centre.

clue.text: Soul mate occasionally abandoned God

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter of the word mate
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A spiritual partner is now and then forsaken by God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes AE from mate; 'abandoned' mixes those with SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he is the keeper of the winds, a deity, so he is an example of a god.

clue.text: A hundred up before Thom Yorke finally gets out

indicators.note: before means this piece comes ahead of the next
up in a down clue means the piece is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word Yorke

explanation.surface: A Radiohead fan reports Thom Yorke leaving after scoring a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A hundred up' is cricket for scoring a century; here 'up' turns A TON over to NOTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Out and away from one's house are the same thing, as when a caller is told the person is away.

clue.text: Watch on for Canal+ live broadcast

parts.note: Canal+ is a French TV channel, so on is given in French, sur

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Tuning in to a live broadcast on the French channel Canal+.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal+' signals French, hence SUR; 'broadcast' turns LIVE into VEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep under surveillance is to observe closely, a synonym of watch as a verb.

clue.text: Amused fielder corrected Strauss's score

indicators.note: corrected means the letters are put right in a different order

explanation.surface: A fielder, amused, corrects the scorer on the cricket match total.
explanation.walkthrough: The operetta's German title means The Bat, tying it to the 25 theme.
explanation.definitionFit: This operetta by Johann Strauss II is one of his scores, so the clue's description names it.

clue.text: Italian writer embracing hot nymph

indicators.note: embracing means the writer's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Umberto Eco was the Italian novelist of The Name of the Rose
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An Italian author is caught in a passionate clinch with a mythical nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the nymph pined for Narcissus until only her voice remained, so she is a named example of a nymph.

clue.text: Hector and Paris almost lost 25

indicators.note: lost means the letters have gone astray and must be put back in a new order
almost means the last letter of Paris is dropped

explanation.surface: Two Trojan princes, Hector and Paris, nearly lose a battle against flying mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Paris to PARI; 'lost' scrambles HECTOR plus PARI into the scientific order name. 25 is BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the zoological order containing every bat species, so it is the scientific name for the animals.

clue.text: Authority inspector boarding boat

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so one piece goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed river boat
DI is short for Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A senior official climbs aboard a boat to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: A punt is a flat-bottomed boat pushed with a pole, common on rivers at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert commentator is someone regarded as an authority, a synonym in the sense of a knowledgeable person.

clue.text: Is that aubergine emoji rude or ultimately more salacious?

parts.note: an aubergine (eggplant) is botanically a fruit

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of each of the words emoji, rude and or

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if the suggestive eggplant emoji is rude or simply racier than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of 'emoji rude or', giving IER after the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruity can mean suggestive or risqué, so the comparative form means more lewd or suggestive.

clue.text: Enclose page to guide bureaucrat

parts.note: to pen is to shut in or enclose
to usher is to guide someone to a seat

explanation.surface: Instructions to fold a page into an envelope to direct an office official.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk clerk doing routine paperwork is a disparaging term for an office functionary.

clue.text: Curtly spotted pinching Eagle Annual

indicators.note: pinching means taking hold of, so the bird goes inside
curtly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pimply means covered in spots
an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a pimply teenager pinching the Eagle comic annual.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eagle was a British boys' comic with yearly annuals, so 'Annual' looks like a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet variety is a flowering plant that completes its life cycle in one year, an annual.

clue.text: Book stars to return on 1st of January

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece
the first letter of the word January is taken
to return means the star sign is read backwards

parts.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A reader schedules the return of a library book about astronomy for New Year's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the minor prophets, a short book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Celebrity lover's out of line

indicators.note: out of means the line letter is removed from the word

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover

explanation.surface: A famous person's partner has stepped out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity and renown both mean the state of being widely known, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Stick with cool group of admirers

parts.note: to fan is to cool
a club is a stick used as a weapon

explanation.surface: Sticking with the cool crowd of fans.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised society of devotees of a star or team is a group of people who admire them.

clue.text: Drink with pop star Lola Young primarily educational

parts.note: tea is a common drink
Cher is the American pop singer

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of Lola and Young

explanation.surface: Having a cuppa with two singers sounds like an educational outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lola Young is a real British singer, so the clue looks like a list of pop names.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something befitting an instructor, so it has the sense of instructive or pedagogic.

clue.text: Lord's speciality jumper

definitions.meaning: Lord's is the famous London ... ground, so the sport played there
a jumping insect like a grasshopper

explanation.surface: A peer's speciality is said to be a knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, while 'jumper' looks like a British sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the sport played at Lord's and also a chirping insect that leaps.

clue.text: Captain regularly tucking into brief meal and fruitcake

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside the meal
brief means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: lunch is a meal

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word Captain

explanation.surface: A captain regularly tucks into a quick lunch and some fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives ATI from Captain; 'brief' cuts LUNCH to LUNC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, so it means a madman.

clue.text: Month before summer yielding more nuts

indicators.note: before means placed ahead in this down clue

parts.note: someone who sums, an adder, is a summer

explanation.surface: The month before summer brings a bigger harvest of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who sums, i.e. an adder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts means crazy, so the comparative of mad is crazier.

clue.text: Member following EU articles for controversial delivery method?

indicators.note: following means the limb comes after the articles

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article and der the German definite one, both EU languages
der is a German definite article
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Euro politician weighs in on a disputed way of delivering something.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an underarm ball is notorious: an underarm delivery in a 1981 one-day match caused a famous row.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling with the hand below shoulder height is the delivery style, with the question mark flagging the cricket sense.

clue.text: Salvation Army entering pub before 9.25

indicators.note: before means the pub piece comes ahead of the next letter
entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
9 across is Echo, the NATO alphabet word for the letter E

explanation.surface: Charity workers arrive at a pub shortly before closing time, 9.25 pm.
explanation.walkthrough: The time 9.25 is really two cross-references: 9 is ECHO, standing for E, and 25 is BATS, slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crazy, slang 'bats', is a synonym for out of one's mind.

clue.text: One of the greatest employers of 1825 almost entirely abstemious

indicators.note: almost entirely means the whole name but its last letter

parts.words: One of the greatest employers of 1825
parts.note: Garry Sobers, the West Indian, was one of the greatest users of cricket bats (18 and 25)

explanation.surface: A famous Victorian employer of 1825 was nearly a teetotaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 1825 reads like a year but is 18 and 25: CRICKET BATS. Garry Sobers was a great West Indian cricket all-rounder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being temperate and drinking no alcohol, sober and abstemious are synonyms.

clue.text: Swedish opera singer with doctor in bed getting slaughtered

indicators.note: in means the singer and doctor go inside the bed

parts.note: a bunk is a bed
Jenny Lind was the Swedish soprano

explanation.surface: A soprano and her doctor are found in bed, both murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughtered is British slang for very drunk, an idiom equivalent to legless.

clue.text: Super Furry Animals attempt to make a comeback

indicators.note: to make a comeback means the word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a stab is an attempt

explanation.surface: The Welsh band Super Furry Animals try to reunite for a comeback tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Super Furry Animals is a real Welsh rock band, but here the words just describe furry flying animals.
explanation.definitionFit: These nocturnal mammals are covered in fur, so the band's name describes them playfully.

clue.text: Outspoken Beauty liberated in part of tower

indicators.note: outspoken means the words are spoken, so what is heard gives the entry

parts.note: a belle is a beauty and liberated means free

explanation.surface: A frank beauty is finally freed from her prison in a castle tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Belle plus free, said together, gives the bell chamber, a favourite roost for bats.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the room in a church tower where the bells hang, so it is one section of a tower.

clue.text: Sadly, the eminent Royal Institution chemist starts applying to atomic organisation

indicators.note: starts means the initial letters of the six words from Sadly to chemist

explanation.surface: A lament that a celebrated Royal Institution chemist began working on the structure of atoms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Institution is a London science body famous for its Christmas lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the spatial arrangement of atoms in a molecule, as in steric hindrance.
